In that video, I kept a constant turn rate at the best corner velocity. All of my opponent's attempts to gimbal, z thrust, and disable FA were met with a stalemate. If I had not missed my recharge, I could have stayed in that fight. No you don't! The entire point of FA off is that all your inertia is additive instead of absolute. You have full control over your momentum. Granted, it is much harder to keep control and this is part of the learning curve I spoke of earlier.

At the end of the day, the most important part of combat manoeuvring is to keep your weapons in their firing range for longer than your opponent while keeping out of their firing envelope

...which is where circle strafing comes in, and really it's just the tip of the iceburg. "Tail chasing" (you spend the majority of your combat time in this video doing this) is the first technique players learn for combat, because it's the easiest and the most intuitive. If both players are tail chasing, the person with the better turning rate wins. The problem is you're limiting your manoeuvres to only the most basic things - there's a deeper level of play that can be achieved if you master some techniques. Of course, this is extremely difficult, if not impossible to pull off with a mouse and keyboard.

The biggest problem a lot of players have with elite is that they see it as being "fighter jets in space". However, if you start using Newtonian physics as it relates to space to your advantage there's a lot more that can be done.

You inertia does become additive, but your vector is no longer coupled to your heading and your absolute speed reduces with each vector change of more than 90°.

I would like for the game to require complex maneuvers to get a firing solution, but it isn't balanced that way.

Here is how I look at it. If I gimbal, I can get guns on target, but I risk being a sitting duck for anyone who puts my vector in their cross hairs. If I gimbal, I hurt my ability to break their firing solution. Instead of rolling on my y axis and breaking into my opponent at max velocity to break up their firing solution, with FA off I have to add velocity from a relative 0 to accomplish the same thing.

Having said that, I wish Frontier would create areas with real challenge that demanded true pilot skills to be successful. PvE is basically seal clubbing, and PvP is too rare to rely on for constant action.
